narrative:
The model determined that you have a 41% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the loan amount you requested, and your property ownership situation. Your checking account balance in the 0-200 DM range was the most important reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only 18% have this same modest balance level, while nearly 60% have no checking account at all. This status pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk.

The second most influential factor was the amount of credit you asked for. At 4,297 DM, your request is higher than the average of about 3,020 DM seen among those who were approved. Surprisingly, this larger amount actually worked slightly in your favor and pulled the prediction a little toward approval.

Finally, having no known property or assets was the third strongest driver. This characteristic is relatively uncommon and pushed the decision further toward viewing you as higher risk.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude you fall on the wrong side of the risk line. To improve your chances next time, focus on building a stronger checking account balance and consider applying for a smaller loan amount. You may also want to explore ways to document or acquire assets that could strengthen your profile.
